finding.claim: The /invoice/<inv_id> route has no authentication and no ownership check (IDOR / missing authorization). Any caller can read any customer's invoice by ID. The sibling route /my/invoice/<inv_id> does check ownership, which shows the check was intended.
finding.source: URL path parameter inv_id from an unauthenticated HTTP request
finding.sink: jsonify(inv) returns the full invoice record from INVOICES

trace.note: Route registered with no auth decorator or before_request guard
Invoice looked up by request-supplied ID only; no comparison of inv['customer'] to g.user['id']
Full invoice returned to the caller

finding.guards_checked: Checked for decorators, before_request hooks and a customer/tenant comparison. None exist in the file, and it is the only file in the directory. The /my/invoice route at line 16 does enforce ownership, but this route does not. Precondition: the attacker can reach the app and knows or guesses an invoice ID. IDs are unknown, and if they are sequential or guessable the exposure is greater.

verdict.reason: invoices.py:7-10 registers /invoice/<inv_id> with no decorator, before_request hook, or ownership check and returns jsonify(inv) for any ID, unlike invoices.py:16, where /my/invoice/<inv_id> compares inv["customer"] to g.user["id"].
